name: Side-Lying External Rotation
description: The side-lying dumbbell external rotation is a classic rotator cuff exercise performed lying on one side, rotating a dumbbell upward from a position of internal rotation to external rotation with the elbow bent to 90 degrees. The gravity-resisted motion precisely isolates the infraspinatus and teres minor throughout the full range, as the body position eliminates most compensatory movements. It is widely prescribed for rotator cuff rehabilitation and shoulder health maintenance.

execution.starting_position: Lie on one side with the bottom arm supporting the head. Hold a light dumbbell in the top hand with the elbow bent to 90 degrees and the forearm pointing toward the floor (internally rotated position).
execution.setup_instructions: Use extremely light dumbbells — 2.5-5 lbs is typically sufficient. A small rolled towel under the elbow can help maintain proper positioning.
steps: Step 1: Lie on your side, top elbow bent at 90 degrees, forearm pointing to the floor.
Step 2: Keep the elbow against the side of the torso throughout.
Step 3: Rotate the forearm upward toward the ceiling (external rotation).
Step 4: Rotate as far as comfortable — typically until the forearm is perpendicular to the floor or slightly past.
Step 5: Lower slowly back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe naturally throughout — this is a low-load exercise.
common_mistakes: Using too heavy a dumbbell — technique breaks down immediately
Letting the elbow drift away from the body during rotation
safety_considerations: If there is any pain in the shoulder, stop immediately and consult a healthcare professional
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: From internal rotation (forearm toward floor) to external rotation (forearm toward ceiling, up to 90 degrees of rotation).
coaching_cues: Elbow stays at your side — only the forearm moves
This is rehab work — quality over load
